newsitem.title: USA: Clinton hopes to end hospital stay on Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hopes to end hospital stay on Sunday.

text.p: Workers were readying the White House for President Clinton's expected return on Sunday, trying to make it easier for a man on crutches to navigate the executive mansion.

Despite experiencing some sharp pain on Saturday, the day after undergoing emergency surgery to repair a torn tendon on his right knee, Clinton planned to be discharged from Bethesda National Naval Medical Centre in suburban Maryland by Sunday afternoon, aides said.

First lady Hillary Rodham Clinton, who delayed the start of her trip to Africa, led a physical therapist on a tour of the White House on Saturday to determine what changes would be needed to make life easier and safer for a president on crutches.

"They walked literally room by room ... and located furniture that's going to have to be moved and rugs that are going to have to be taped down and some of the physical adjustments they'll have to make," Press Secretary Mike McCurry said.
Facing a summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Wednesday in Helsinki, Clinton was anxious to return to the White House as soon as possible, McCurry said.
"He really wants to go home tomorrow and plans to go home tomorrow," McCurry told reporters at a late Saturday afternoon briefing.

McCurry said there has been no discussion of delaying or significantly altering Clinton's plans for the two-day summit with Yeltsin -- whose own health has been more of a concern than that of the 50-year-old president.

A member of the medical team that operated on Clinton was expected to accompany him to the summit, along with a physical therapist and the physicans who routinely accompany a president on foreign trips.
Clinton tore his tendon in a freak accident on Friday when he lost his footing on a step at the Florida home of Australian golf professional Greg Norman.
His knee buckled, tearing the quadriceps tendon connecting the kneecap to the upper thigh in his right leg. He was flown back to Washington and operated on at the Bethesda hospital.
The accident forced postponement of a planned White House visit by Jordan's King Hussein that had been set for Tuesday.

If discharged on Sunday, Clinton planned a limited Monday schedule -- a brief session with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, who is in Washington to prepare for the summit, and a farewell exchange with Walter Mondale, the former vice president who is stepping down as U.S. ambassador to Japan.
Clinton will forgo the traditional St. Patrick's Day meeting with a senior Irish official. Prime Minister John Bruton, instead, will meet with Gore.
Mrs. Clinton, who had planned to leave on Saturday for a two-week tour of Africa, instead planned to depart (on) Sunday afternoon.
Jordan's King Hussein postponed his plans to meet with Clinton on Tuesday for talks about Middle East peace efforts.
